title: Minimax Inference for Normalized Continuous-Dose Gibbs Policy Welfare
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; projected paper score 5.8 < 7.4 and NOT salvageable in scope.
gap_reasons: The delivered content is a matched two-regime estimation and honest-length theorem for one fixed sixteen-dimensional, known-design, single-peak class. Its additional contribution is a narrow normalized-functional specialization of established [quadratic-functional machinery](https://jmlr.org/papers/v22/19-892.html) and [endogenous softmax differentiation](https://arxiv.org/html/2507.11780v2), rather than a broadly applicable inference framework. The unique curved peak and fixed exterior gap exclude competing dose regimes and near-tied maxima, leaving the prospective application relevance confined to a restrictive benchmark. The certificate establishes computability, but its absent runtime bound, potentially enormous threshold, and symbolic singleton-repair example leave practical informativeness unestablished. The TL;DR's matched-rate and coverage claims track the delivered statements; the subfield tier and 5.8 score reflect limited significance and operational evidence, not a missing converse or an undisclosed open theorem. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 5.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'subfield' is capped at 'incremental'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

proof_attempt_summary: Four D0 solve rounds developed the finite-arithmetic certificate and expanded the matched RMSE/honest-length result to alpha in [1/70,1/22], with a quadratic/first-order elbow at 1/36. Citation attestations were resolved from the primary PDF; D0.5 assessed incremental novelty and a 5.8 projected score, below the field floor, and an independent gate agreed no bounded same-scope repair would clear it. No Lean formalization was attempted; the quadratic-identity typo and three redundant nodes remain disclosed, while a two-peak program would require a new proposal anchor and new upper-bound proofs.
tldr:
For the population-oracle normalized continuous-dose Gibbs welfare \(W(m)\), the unchanged sixteen-dimensional bounded Bernoulli class has matched minimax RMSE and connected honest-interval expected-length order
\(\rho_n(\alpha)=\max\{n^{-3/7}h^{-38/7},(nh^{16})^{-1/2}\}\), \(h=n^{-\alpha}\), over the endpoint-inclusive public window \([1/70,1/22]\).
The quadratic branch governs \([1/70,1/36]\), and the adjacent first-order branch governs \([1/36,1/22]\).
One data-only unknown-mode polynomial pilot, signed second-order twicing statistic with both normalization ranks, and extended finite-arithmetic certificate attain both branches with coverage at least \(9/10\) for every finite sample size.
Legal packed original Bernoulli mixtures and a localized original-Bernoulli two-point experiment supply the respective converses, including connected honest length at the quadratic baseline.
The lower bounds transfer to legal smoothness superclasses; upper attainment remains on \(\mathcal H\).
This is a normalized-functional specialization of established quadratic-functional and higher-order machinery.
gap: The inspected ADRF/QDRF, fixed-treatment HOIF, incremental-exposure, and finite-action softmax results establish important localization, normalization, and inference machinery. Their cited theorems do not supply the joint same-class RMSE and connected honest-length frontier for the shrinking outcome-endogenous continuous-action welfare \(W(m)\) in this original Bernoulli experiment. This is a distinct-target comparison, not a claim of a faster generic rate.
fill: The requested theorem couples a class-legal original-law converse with unknown-mode localization and an observable finite-sample reporting procedure. The feasible upper bound and the field case require a completed \texttt{oeq:finite-certificate}, including certified input, integration, and rounding errors. Generic quadratic-functional rates, sample splitting, projection U-statistics, HOIF bias correction, testing-to-length arguments, and softmax derivatives are credited. Failure of the finite certificate or an affirmative same-kernel comparator theorem defeats this delivery claim.
